title: Aurora Retail - Redwood Console tracing & request logs walkthrough
summary: Redwood AE+SE walked Aurora through Console tracing, error analysis, and request logs. Customer concerned about noisy errors, debug flows for production incidents, and private deployment/VPC logging. Agreed to run a short benchmark and share security docs and sample logs. Next steps include follow-up pilot plan and pricing from AE.
next_steps: Priya to share demo recording and tracing quickstart doc (by 2027-01-04)
Jordan to send pricing for 3-month pilot and Dedicated capacity options (by 2027-01-06)
Maya to provide sample failing request IDs for live debugging session (by 2027-01-03)
Schedule 1-hr pilot kickoff once sample logs shared
action_items: Priya Nair | Share tracing quickstart + playbook | 2027-01-04
Jordan Lee | Quote for 3-month pilot and Dedicated commit options | 2027-01-06
Maya Patel | Send sample request IDs and a short repro script | 2027-01-03
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Jordan from Redwood AE, with Priya on the call for the demo. Uh quick intro, then we'll jump into the console.
[00:12] Sam Chen: Thanks Jordan, we got a short agenda: tracing, error analysis, and request logs — especially how you'd debug noisy failures in production.
[00:23] Priya Nair: Great. I'll share my screen, give me one sec. (screen share noise) Okay you should see the Redwood Console home, this is the environment we've pre-populated with a sample app called aurora-recs.
[00:40] Maya Patel: Looks good, the naming is similar to our internal names which helps.
[00:47] Priya Nair: Cool. First up tracing: we surface a per-request trace that ties the API call, routing decision, model variant used, batch id, and the GPU node. So if a request timed out you can click into the trace and see where latency spiked.
[01:05] Liam O'Neil: Do you capture KV cache hits? A lot of our tail latency seems kv-cache related.
[01:12] Priya Nair: Yeah, we include prefix/KV cache metrics in the trace. You'll see a block that shows cache hit/miss and the cache lookup time. Note sometimes the auto-generated names for kernels show as, uh, "conv-opt-512" or similar — transcription may be off there in logs — but the timing is accurate.
[01:35] Jordan Lee: Important for Aurora is the ability to filter traces by model version, route, tenant, and by error class. So you can isolate a spike to either a model variant or infra.
[01:47] Maya Patel: Can we export traces for offline analysis? We want to feed them into our internal APM.
[01:53] Priya Nair: Yes, you can export JSON lines via the request logs endpoint or download from the UI. We'll share the quickstart doc.
[02:05] Jordan Lee: Quick note on privacy — for Private deployments we can ship the control plane inside your VPC and logs stay in your account; for Hosted the logs are retained per plan and we provide SOC2 reports.
[02:20] Sam Chen: Sounds good. Our security team will want KMS and HSM details, but we can get that in the follow-up.
[02:27] Priya Nair: Absolutely. Moving on, error analysis: Console surfaces a consolidated errors page where you can group by error message, HTTP status, or model error.
[02:40] Priya Nair: Example here, we have a cluster of 502-like errors that actually come from OOM on a quantized model variant — the trace shows the GPU OOM event, then the fallback route that returned a smaller model.
[02:54] Maya Patel: That's interesting. How does fallback impact response semantics? If you fallback to a smaller model does the output format stay consistent?
[03:02] Carlos Mendes: Good question. We support structured output and schema checks. Fallbacks are configured to use compatible model variants so for most schema-constrained outputs the shape is preserved; we flag potential quality regressions in the telemetry.
[03:18] Liam O'Neil: Do you have alerts? We need to know when error clusters cross thresholds.
[03:23] Priya Nair: Yes, you can configure alerts on error rate, latency SLO breaches, and quality regressions tied to eval prompt sets. Alerts integrate with PagerDuty/Slack.
[03:34] Maya Patel: How granular are request logs? We need full request+response for debugging but also want redaction for PII.
[03:42] Priya Nair: Logs are fully plumbed — request payload, headers (optional), response, model logits if enabled — but you can configure redaction rules and retention windows. For Private deploys we can also plug into your KMS for envelope encryption.
[03:58] Sam Chen: Okay if we pull logs to our S3, what format is it and how large?
[04:05] Priya Nair: It's ndjson, each line a single request event with trace id, timestamps, route, model_id, worker_id, and payloads optionally. File sizes depend on tokens, but we've got sampling and include/exclude rules to reduce volume.
[04:20] Jordan Lee: For the debugging flow, let's do a live example. Maya, you mentioned you had a failing request earlier?
[04:27] Maya Patel: Yes, we have a set of failing request IDs — I pasted three into the shared doc, but I only copied the first one into the chat. It's request id: 9f4c2a7b.
[04:37] Priya Nair: Great, I'll search by request id in the console. (typing) Found it. The trace shows a 504 gateway timeout with a long queuing time before execution.
[04:50] Priya Nair: See here — there's a burst on that particular route that caused batching to grow beyond the latency SLO, plus the model variant used is a larger quantized variant which had a longer kernel init.
[05:05] Maya Patel: Hmm, kernel init times — can you show the kernel timing breakdown?
[05:10] Priya Nair: Sure, under the trace details, kernel times are listed per step. There's a 180ms init followed by 360ms token generation. You can see a hint where we recommend switching to a warm-up pool or using a smaller model during bursts.
[05:27] Jordan Lee: We also have intelligent routing: you can set rules to route high-priority traffic to dedicated capacity to avoid noisy neighbor burst effects, or set a fallback lower-cost variant for best-effort requests.
[05:40] Sam Chen: For cost reasons we prefer to keep most traffic on hosted but want guaranteed performance for checkout flows. Is that easy to configure?
[05:48] Carlos Mendes: Yes, create route-based policies: checkout-route -> dedicated, low-latency; recs-route -> hosted with cache and batching settings tuned. The Console shows per-route cost and latency so you can validate.
[06:02] Maya Patel: About sampling — can we sample 100% for a short window during incidents?
[06:07] Priya Nair: Yep, you can change sampling in the Console or via API. There's also an endpoint to pull full logs for a time range.
[06:16] Liam O'Neil: Any rate limits during export? We need to do full dumps for forensic analysis.
[06:21] Priya Nair: For Private customers we can coordinate high-throughput export paths; for hosted there's an export quota but we can provision higher throughputs for pilot periods.
[06:33] Jordan Lee: Quick sidebar: we have a diagnostics bundle feature that collects traces, host metrics, and request logs for a given time window — safe to share with our SEs.
[06:45] Maya Patel: Nice. That will speed root-cause analysis.
[06:50] Priya Nair: Moving to error taxonomy — Console tries to classify errors as infra, model, or request-level. Sometimes the classifier mislabels things (transcription error in logs might show "modle" instead of model) but you can drill down.
[07:05] Maya Patel: Do you surface regression alerts when a new model version increases error rate?
[07:10] Priya Nair: Yes, quality monitoring ties to prompt sets. You can run canaries per model and get alerts when mismatch or degradation exceeds thresholds.
[07:20] Sam Chen: For our compliance team, can we redact PII automatically before sending logs to external tools?
[07:25] Priya Nair: You can set redaction rules — regex-based for emails/phone numbers and schema-based redaction for structured fields. We'll share the doc with examples.
[07:36] Jordan Lee: Let's demo a debugging scenario end-to-end: search by trace id, inspect timeline, view request log, then reproduce via the replay feature. Priya walk us through.
[07:46] Priya Nair: On the trace page click "Replay request" — it replays the request through a sandboxed route that uses the same model variant and records a new trace. This helps validate fixes without affecting production.
[08:00] Maya Patel: Is replay isolated? We don't want side effects like writes to downstream systems.
[08:04] Priya Nair: Replay is sandboxed and strips side-effectful headers by default. You can configure a mock downstream or disable external calls.
[08:13] Liam O'Neil: What about request signing and auth when replaying?
[08:17] Priya Nair: Replay uses a replay token that you generate in the Console and can scope to routes. It respects RBAC so only authorized users can replay.
[08:29] Sam Chen: Ok that covers debugging features. Quick question on observability: do you expose token-level cost data in traces?
[08:36] Carlos Mendes: Yes we show per-token compute time and token counts in the trace, which maps back to per-request cost. That helps optimize prompts and batching.
[08:46] Maya Patel: We do a lot of templating and system prompts — can we test prompt regressions?
[08:50] Priya Nair: We integrate with Redwood Optimize: you can run A/B evals against prompt sets and get quality delta and cost tradeoffs. We'll include a Optimize starter guide.
[09:02] Jordan Lee: Time check — we've been live for ~9 minutes, we have ~33 left. Any specific deep-dive requests?
[09:09] Maya Patel: Can you show the raw ndjson log for that earlier request?
[09:13] Priya Nair: Sure. (opens logs) Here's the ndjson entry: {"trace_id":"9f4c2a7b","ts":"2026-12-30T14:42:31Z","route":"recs-v2","model":"recs-quant-v2","tokens":128,"latency_ms":920,"error":"gateway_timeout"} — note in the UI we pretty-print but the export is ndjson.
[09:36] Jordan Lee: In the logs you can also see worker_id and GPU id; sometimes the worker id gets truncated in the UI because of the display width — the raw export keeps full ids.
[09:46] Maya Patel: Can you show an example of a modeled regression alert?
[09:50] Priya Nair: (click) Here's an alert — model v3 had a +12% increase in hallucination rate on our eval set after a patch; the quality dashboard links to the failing prompts and the diffs in outputs.
[10:05] Sam Chen: How do you define hallucination in the dashboard?
[10:09] Priya Nair: It's user-defined: we compare outputs to a ground truth or golden set and compute semantic similarity thresholds; you can tune the threshold per eval.
[10:18] Maya Patel: Any auto-rollbacks?
[10:20] Carlos Mendes: We have automatic fallback to previous version if a canary crosses a threshold, or you can configure canary policies to pause rollout.
[10:29] Maya Patel: For our infra, we use GCP in us-central1; do you recommend regional Dedicated pools to reduce cross-region egress?
[10:37] Jordan Lee: Yes, you can pin routes to region-specific capacity. For low-latency checkout regionally colocated Dedicated is recommended.
[10:46] Liam O'Neil: One more: how do you handle retained logs for GDPR concerns?
[10:50] Priya Nair: Retention windows are configurable per-tenant; for european customers we support EU-only storage and we can set minimal retention or automatic purge policies.
[11:00] Maya Patel: Great. Let's talk pilot scope — we want to run a 3-week pilot on our recs-route with 1k qps simulated burst, keep checkout on a tiny dedicated pool.
[11:10] Jordan Lee: That sounds achievable. We'll propose a pilot plan: Hosted with a small Dedicated pool for checkout, sampling at 100% for the recs-route during incident windows, and a benchmark run to validate latency SLOs.
[11:21] Sam Chen: Pricing?
[11:24] Jordan Lee: I'll send a pilot quote. For cost sanity you can enable caching and lower-cost quantized variants for the recs traffic; we'll include cost modeling in the proposal.
[11:36] Maya Patel: Any gotchas we should be aware of?
[11:39] Priya Nair: A couple: cold-start kernel init can increase tail latency if warms are not configured; also sampling at 100% raises log volume quickly so plan exports accordingly.
[11:51] Carlos Mendes: Also watch out for very large system prompts that increase token counts and push you into a larger kernel path — the console flags those in the trace.
[12:05] Liam O'Neil: For the sample failing request, can we set up a live debugging session next week?
[12:10] Jordan Lee: Yes, propose times and we'll get Priya and Carlos on the call.
[12:16] Sam Chen: Thanks, useful overview. One more ask — can you share a sample diagnostics bundle we can ingest?
[12:22] Priya Nair: We'll attach a sanitized sample bundle to the follow-up email.
[12:28] Maya Patel: Perfect.
[12:30] Jordan Lee: Recap of next steps — Priya share demo assets and quickstart, Jordan send pilot pricing, Maya send request IDs and repro. We'll schedule pilot kickoff once sample logs are ingested.
[12:45] Sam Chen: Sounds good, thanks everyone.
[12:48] Jordan Lee: Thanks all, we'll follow up.
[12:50] (call ends)

Notes: Transcript contains small transcription artifacts and occasional mis-typed product names (e.g., "KV cache" sometimes shown as "kv-cache" or mis-spelled kernel names). Shared doc link: https://redwood.ai/samples/aurora-recs-demo (placeholder). Security pack link: https://redwood.ai/security/soc2 (placeholder).
